==English== ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/dɪˈbeɪt/|a=UK}} * {{IPA|en|/dɪˈbeɪt/|/di-/|/də-/|a=US}} * {{audio|en|En-us-debate.ogg|a=GA}} * {{rhymes|en|eɪt|s=2}} ===Etymology 1=== From {{inh|en|enm|debaten}}, from {{der|en|fro|debatre||to fight, contend, debate, also literally to beat down}}, from Romanic {{m|und||desbattere}}, from {{der|en|la|dis-||apart, in different directions}} + {{m|la|battuō||to beat, to fence}}. ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|ambitransitive|reciprocal}} To [[participate]] in a debate; to [[dispute]], [[argue]], especially in a public arena. {{defdate|from 14th c.}} #: {{syn|en|contend|canvass}} #: {{ux|en|"'''Debate''' me, coward!" snarled the completely normal intellectual.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 8|II|iv|passage=a wise council {{...}} that did '''debate''' this business}} #* {{RQ:KJV|Proverbs|25|9||'''Debate''' thy cause with thy neighbour himself.}} #* {{RQ:Tatler|53|August 11, 1709 |passage=He presents that great soul '''debating''' upon the subject of life and death with his intimate friends.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete|intransitive|reciprocal}} To [[fight]]. {{defdate|14th|17th c.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1609|author=w:William Shakespeare|title=Sonnet 15|text={{...}} wasteful Time '''debateth''' with Decay,
To change your day of youth to sullied night}} # {{lb|en|obsolete|transitive}} To engage in combat for; to strive for. #* {{RQ:Prescott Ferdinand and Isabella|passage=Volunteers {{...}} thronged to serve under his banner, and the cause of religion was '''debated''' with the same ardour in Spain as on the plains of Palestine.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[consider]] (to oneself), to [[think]] over, to attempt to [[decide]] #: {{ux|en|He was '''debating''' where he'd spend his holiday.}} =====Derived terms===== {{col|en|debater|debatability|debatable,debateable|outdebate|redebate|debatingly|undebating|mass debate}} =====Related terms===== {{col3|en|debation|debatable|combat|batter|battle|abate|battery}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top|participate in a debate}} * Albanian: * Armenian: * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Chinese: * Czech: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * French: * Georgian: * German: * Greek: * Hindi: * Hungarian: * Ido: * Italian: * Khmer: * Korean: * Latin: * Latvian: * Māori: * Mongolian: * Persian: * Portuguese: * Russian: {{t+|ru|дискути́ровать}}, {{t+|ru|спори́ть}}, {{t+|ru|обсужда́ть}} * Scottish Gaelic: * Spanish: * Swahili: * Swedish: * Telugu: * Thai: * Turkish: * Ukrainian: * Vietnamese: * Welsh: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|To consider to oneself}} * Italian: * Māori: {{trans-bottom}} ===Etymology 2=== From {{inh|en|enm|debat}}, {{bor+|enm|fro|debat|nocat=1|nocap=1}}, [[deverbal]] of {{m|fro|debatre}}, see [[#Etymology 1|Etymology 1]] for more. ====Noun==== {{en-noun|~}} # An [[argument]], or [[discussion]], usually in an ordered or formal setting, often with more than two people, generally ending with a [[vote]] or other decision. #: {{ux|en|After a four-hour '''debate''', the committee voted to table the motion.}} # An informal and spirited but generally civil discussion of opposing views. #: {{ux|en|The '''debate''' over the age of the universe is thousands of years old.}} #: {{ux|en|There was a bit of a '''debate''' over who should pay for the damaged fence.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-07-26|author=w:Leo Hickman |volume=189|issue=7|page=26|magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly |title=[http://www.theguardian.com/science/2013/jul/01/how-algorithms-rule-world-nsa How algorithms rule the world] |passage=The use of algorithms in policing is one example of their increasing influence on our lives. And, as their ubiquity spreads, so too does the '''debate''' around whether we should allow ourselves to become so reliant on them – and who, if anyone, is policing their use.}} # {{lb|en|uncountable}} Discussion of opposing views. #: {{ux|en|There has been considerable '''debate''' concerning exactly how to format these articles.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|year=2013|month=September-October|author=[http://www.americanscientist.org/authors/detail/katie-l-burke Katie L. Burke]| magazine=w:American Scientist|title=[http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/pub/2013/5/in-the-news-47 In the News]| passage=Oxygen levels on Earth skyrocketed 2.4 billion years ago, when cyanobacteria evolved photosynthesis:{{...}}. The evolutionary precursor of photosynthesis is still under '''debate''', and a new study sheds light. The critical component of the photosynthetic system is the “water-oxidizing complex”, made up of manganese atoms and a calcium atom.}} # {{lb|en|frequently in the French form ''débat''}} A type of literary composition, taking the form of a discussion or disputation, commonly found in the [[vernacular]] medieval poetry of many European countries, as well as in [[wikipedia:medieval Latin|medieval Latin]]. # {{lb|en|obsolete}} [[strife|Strife]], [[discord]]. =====Derived terms=====
